html:
Uganda is a landlocked country in East Africa, on the north shore of Lake Victoria. On the map it runs from the British protectorate of 1894 to the republic of today.

The country takes its name from Buganda, the strongest of several kingdoms in the area, alongside Bunyoro, Toro and Ankole. Arab and Swahili traders had reached the court of Buganda by the 1840s and missionaries followed. Religious rivalry at court led to the killing of the Uganda Martyrs in 1885 to 1887.

Britain declared a protectorate in 1894. A 1900 agreement left Buganda its king, the Kabaka, and much of its land, and Britain ruled through local chiefs. The Uganda Railway from Mombasa reached the lake in 1901, and cotton became the main export.

After independence the story turned violent:

  • 1962: independence, with Milton Obote as prime minister.
  • 1966: Obote's army stormed the Kabaka's palace; the kingdoms were abolished the next year.
  • 1971: Idi Amin seized power. In 1972 he expelled the Asian community. His rule killed very large numbers of people.
  • 1979: after Amin invaded Tanzania, Tanzanian troops and Ugandan exiles drove him out.
  • 1980 to 1986: Obote's second rule and a bush war.
  • 1986: Yoweri Museveni took Kampala. He has ruled since.

The old kingdoms came back in 1993 as cultural bodies without political power. In the 1990s Uganda became known for an open campaign against the AIDS epidemic, which had struck it early and hard.
sum: Uganda is a landlocked country in East Africa, on the north shore of Lake Victoria. On the map it runs from the British protectorate of 1894 to the republic of today.
